wbg_operations.title: Housing Finance, Lands and Sustainable Investments
wbg_operations.amount_basis: World Bank original commitment (USD), whole operation; not allocated to clusters
wbg_operations.description: The earlier Kenya Affordable Housing Finance Project (KAHFP) (P165034) made significant strides in expanding access to affordable housing finance in Kenya, primarily through the support and operationalization of the Kenya Mortgage Refinance Company (KMRC). As of December 2025, KMRC refinanced approximately KES 25.3 billion in mortgages, representing 5,148 loans. Repayment tenor lengthened from 8.3 (2021) to 12.3 years (2025) signaling enhanced affordability. Notably, nearly 48 percent of KMRC-refinanced mortgages were issued to women, highlighting significant progress in gender inclusion. KMRC’s portfolio now accounts for about 5.0 percent of the banking sector’s mortgage book by value and 12.8 percent by number of loans. Additionally, the share of refinancing through SACCOs within KMRC’s portfolio grew from 7 percent in 2022 to 15.2 percent by December 2025, indicating a strengthened role for non-bank lenders in the affordable housing finance sector and growing financial inclusion. These achievements demonstrate that KMRC is actively driving the market forward in a positive direction; however, affordability remains a binding constraint for the majority. The Housing Finance, Lands and Sustainable Investments Project - is aimed at strengthening the Kenyan housing market by addressing some of the lingering demand and supply gaps in the sector. To ensure continuity, it proposes to support KMRC with a line of credit for mortgage refinancing, blended with KMRC’s own funding raised through bond issuances on the capital markets, to ensure leverage of the IDA/IBRD resources and the overall sustainability of the mortgage market. The project will aim to deliver additionality by moving beyond conventional mortgage financing and exploring more innovative products that can reach underserved segments of the market. It will also support the State Department of Lands and Physical Planning (SDLPP) in its reforms to make property registration faster, cheaper and more reliable, which is a precondition to develop the mortgage market. Additionally, the project proposes to support the Government of Kenya (GoK), via the National Treasury (NT), in launching a sovereign sustainability-linked loan (SLL). The innovative instrument ties the cost of borrowing to national sustainability targets, aligning Kenya’s financing needs with measurable environmental and development outcomes that would also have co-benefits for housing. It will also support a sub-sovereign sustainability bond issuance by KMRC.The four components of the project include: Component 1: Support to KMRC. This component will provide a line of credit to KMRC and ensure continuity and enhanced uptake of the company’s current product offering while innovating to serve unmet market needs. IBRD will provide a credit line to KMRC through the NT to refinance affordable housing loans. As in the first phase of the project, KMRC will extend loans to banks and Savings and Credit Cooperative Organizations (SACCOs) collectively known as Primary Mortgage Lenders (PMLs) that meet strict eligibility criteria. Such loans will be secured against eligible mortgage/housing loans. Moving beyond conventional mortgage financing, KMRC will pilot innovative refinancing products tailored to underserved market segments. These offerings will include microloans, incremental construction lending, and green mortgages and are designed to address affordability, informality, and climate resilience gaps.Component 2: Support to land administration reforms to accelerate affordable housing. This component would support the State Department of Lands and Physical Planning (SDLPP) in its reforms to make property registration faster, cheaper and more reliable, which is a precondition to develop the mortgage market. Building off the technical assistance completed under KAFHP 1, the Project support will be structured into three sub-components: (2.1) enabling the environment for property and mortgage registration through legal and regulatory reforms: supporting the SDLPP to review, harmonize, and enact legislation to support end-to-end digital land transactions and promote consistency across land administration statutes; (2.2) digitization of spatial and land records data, including geodetic improvements: digitizing existing property rights data (titles, deeds, transfer documents, etc.) and graphical spatial data (survey plans, etc.) so that it is fully available in the digital system; and (2.3) enhancing the Ardhisasa land administration management system by addressing systemic issues: improving the system via business process reengineering to simplify processes, enhance automatic data checks, e-signature and other functionality.Component 3: Sustainable Financing Instruments. Subcomponent 3.1: Sovereign Sustainability-Linked Loan involves the development and issuance of a sovereign Sustainability Linked Loan (SLL) program, to leverage the GoK's strong sustainability agenda to diversify investors and access more affordable international capital. Sovereign borrowing in Kenya has been costly, making innovative financing tools such as this more attractive.  Subcomponent 3.2: Sustainability Bond Issuance. Building on the robust framework and market precedent set by sovereign, KMRC is preparing for its inaugural sustainability bond issuance. This approach will enable KMRC to attract a diverse pool of investors and enhance market credibility. The transition to sustainability bonds will also support KMRC’s commitment to environmental and social impact, further strengthening its role in Kenya’s financial ecosystem. The World Bank financing will provide credit enhancements for the sovereign and sub-sovereign issuances.Component 4: Technical Assistance and Project Management: The TA will support Component 1 and overall project management. Activities will cover the development of new product offerings and assess market readiness. It will help define product characteristics and support the development and implementation of roll out plans. The TA will also help operationalize the Kenya Mortgage Guarantee Trust (KMGT), including capacity building and procurement of relevant IT systems. Additionally, the TA will support preparations for future bond issuances through transaction advisory services and consultancy support. This component will also finance project management and related capacity building.
iati_titles: Housing Finance, Lands and Sustainable Investments

wbg_operations.title: Uganda: Uganda-Tanzania Interconnector Project
wbg_operations.amount_basis: World Bank original commitment (USD), whole operation; not allocated to clusters
wbg_operations.sector: Energy and Mineral Resources,Social Sustainability and Inclusion
wbg_operations.description: The Project will mainly comprise construction of a 400 kV double-circuit transmission line (approximately 260 km within Uganda) and associated substations to interconnect Uganda’s power grid with regional networks. The proposed project supports the implementation of a priority connection in the East Africa region and creates conditions for grid expansion in an access-deficit country. It forms an integral part of the East Africa Power Pool (EAPP) backbone transmission grid and enhances the reliability of power interchanges with the Southern Africa Power Pool (SAPP). The proposed line also strengthens interconnections among Nile Equatorial Lake (NEL) countries. Overall, the project supports the objectives of the region’s power pools (SAPP and EAPP) to optimize energy flows, maximize economic trading, increase supply security, and reduce both carbon emissions and the cost of electricity. The transmission line will help achieve benefits from increased access to electricity, sharing of natural resources, more affordable electricity prices, and improved system reliability through regional support.The Project will comprise the following components: (a) Component 1: Construction of approximately 260 km of 400 kV double-circuit transmission line (Wobulenxi-Masaka-Mutukula) and associated substations at Masaka and Wobulenzi (Uganda). (b) Component 2: Environmental and Social Mitigation, supporting implementation of Environmental Management Plans (including biodiversity offsets), Resettlement Action Plans (RAP), and Livelihood Restoration Action Plans (LRAP). (c) Component 3: Project Implementation Support and Institutional Enhancement, including detailed line design, contractor procurement, and supervision. This component will also enhance institutional capacities of relevant utilities and sector institutions for operation of integrated transmission systems and power trade, including capacity building on climate mitigation and adaptation and implementation of a gender action plan to attract, hire, promote, and retain female talent in the energy sector.
iati_titles: Uganda: Uganda-Tanzania Interconnector Project

wbg_operations.title: NORTHEASTERN ROAD-CORRIDOR ASSET MANAGEMENT PROJECT 2
wbg_operations.operation_type: IBRD/IDA or recipient-executed trust fund operation
wbg_operations.amount_basis: World Bank original commitment (USD), whole operation; not allocated to clusters
wbg_operations.description: The proposed project will finance  specific activities from the following two IPF operations i.e. (1) Uganda North-Eastern Road Corridor Asset Management Project (NERAMP) (P125590) which closed on December 31, 2025 – see Component 1 below, and (2) Uganda: Roads and Bridges in the Refugee Hosting Districts/Koboko-Yumbe-Moyo Road Corridor Project (P171339) – see Components 2 and 3 below. 1)	The Northeastern Road-corridor Asset Management Project (NERAMP) in Uganda was established to minimize transport costs, improve road safety, and maintain and enhance road assets through a comprehensive, multi-year infrastructure program. This initiative focuses on the sustainable management and rehabilitation of the key 340 km Tororo–Mbale–Soroti–Lira–Kamdini corridor, which serves as an essential international route linking the Port of Mombasa (Kenya) with South Sudan and the Democratic Republic of Congo via Uganda. The project was divided into two primary sections: Lot 1 (Tororo-Mbale-Soroti, 150.8 km) and Lot 2 (Soroti-Lira-Kamdini, 189.4 km). Due to necessary scope adjustments aimed at ensuring value for money, the original financing was sufficient only for Lot 2 and a small segment of Lot 1, subsequently restructured and renamed Lot 1A. The remaining unfunded portion, designated Lot 1B, is now addressed as component 1 under this project. 2)	The Roads and Bridges in the Refugee Hosting Districts/Koboko-Yumbe-Moyo Road Corridor Project is a significant infrastructure program funded by the World Bank. Its goal is to upgrade roads across northern Uganda’s refugee-hosting districts, which will improve transportation for both refugees and local residents. The project is scheduled to close in 2027. The initiative focuses on better transport links, supporting livelihoods, and carefully managing social and environmental impacts. Specifically, the project aims to improve road connectivity, streamline supply deliveries for refugees and host communities, and strengthen the Ministry of Works and Transport’s management of environmental and social risks. It includes upgrading the 103-kilometer Koboko-Yumbe-Moyo (KYM) road corridor in Uganda’s West Nile Sub-region. At its core, the KYM Project is a key development effort to connect vital areas, enhance infrastructure, and support the large populations of refugees and their hosts in Northern Uganda. After a request from the Government of Uganda for further assistance, additional measures have been introduced: rehabilitating 16 km of town roads and 15 km of access roads in Koboko, Yumbe, and Moyo districts, along with climate-resilient roadside rest areas, weighbridge, and markets construction in each district. These new interventions are now included as components 2 and 3 of this project.Component 1: Climate resilient upgrading of highway corridors - Road rehabilitation, operations and maintenance including institutional support (estimated cost: US$146 million). Activities finance under this component includes the rehabilitation and maintenance of the remaining 150.8 km section of the Tororo - Mbale - Soroti road section, road safety interventions and support to enhance road asset management system. The component will also finance capacity building for managing OPRC contracts and hands-on training for newly graduated interns. These activities will build on and complement the initial NERAMP project activities. (a)	Subcomponent 1.1: Design, Road rehabilitation, performance maintenance and weigh bridge operations (US$128 million): This subcomponent will finance the civil works on the remainder of the Tororo - Mbale- Soroti road (150.8 km) (US$ 128 million) including the dual weighbridge at km 46+700 in Mbale. Out of the US$ 128 million, the rehabilitation and upgrading of the Tororo-Mbale-Soroti road section to climate resilience standards will strengthen the reliability of the road corridor link between South Sudan, parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo, and northern and eastern Uganda to the port of Mombasa strengthening the resilience of the transport network. The works and services attributed to the US$ 128 million will include: (1) the design and rehabilitation of sections of the road corridor to climate resilient standards including the use of engineering and nature-based solutions to address current and projected extreme rainfall and flood events, rising temperatures and drought conditions (US$112.2 million); (2) routine and periodic maintenance of the whole corridor in light of climate risks and hotspots (US$14.8 million); (3) activities such as management of traffic, road safety, climate risk preparedness and response and axle load control measures i.e. weigh bridge operations (US$1 million).  (b)	Subcomponent 1.2: Institutional support through the upgrade of the Road Asset Management System (RAMS), the upgrade of the Traffic Management System (TMS) and mainstream Road Safety Activities (US$5.5 million). The subcomponent will finance (i) A Road Asset Management System and procedures by main streaming climate resilience in the lifecycle of transport asset management (US$ 1 million); (ii) Road safety activities (US$ 2.5 million) and upgrade of the Traffic Management System (TMS) (US$2.0 million). The Traffic Management Systems (TMS) will optimize the road network by utilizing real-time data to monitor traffic and reduce congestion. Key activities under the TMS shall include adaptive signal timing, incident detection and response coordination, ramp metering, dynamic lane/speed management, vehicle/pedestrian tracking, and providing traveler information i.e., (i) Real-Time Monitoring: Using sensors and cameras to monitor traffic conditions and identify issues on highways; (ii) Active Traffic Control: Adjusting traffic signals based on demand, managing ramp meters, and controlling reversible lanes to optimize flow; (iii) Incident Management: Coordinating with law enforcement and emergency services to detect crashes, manage traffic scenes, and clear incidents to restore capacity; (iv) Demand & Flow Management: Implementing dynamic lane use control, variable speed limits, and managing queues to prevent bottlenecks; (v) Information Dissemination: Providing real-time updates to travelers regarding congestion, weather conditions, and travel times; (vi) Data Analysis & Planning: Analyzing historical and real-time data to improve future traffic strategies.The NERAMP parent project prioritized road safety interventions like driver/school sensitization, signage, and enforcement along the Tororo-Kamdini corridor, aiming to reduce accidents, though implementation faced challenges requiring corrective actions and focus on proper road guidance (signage, enforcement) for drivers. This project will enhance road safety by implementing a Safe Systems Approach, which integrates improved infrastructure elements such as walkways, lighting, and bridges, alongside strengthened management of the road network. The Safe System Approach is designed to account for human error and lessen crash severity, with the goal of achieving zero fatalities. Key initiatives include upgrading roundabouts at intersections, constructing separated pedestrian walkways in peri-urban areas, reducing speed limits through the installation of speed humps, and improving intersections with curb extensions to protect vulnerable road users. These activities collectively aim to reduce road traffic injuries and fatalities by building robust road safety management capacity.  (c)	Subcomponent 1.3: Institutional support through a capacity building program (US$2.5 million). This subcomponent will finance (i) Technical Assistance (TA) to strengthen MoWT’s capacity for Design, Procurement, Management and Supervision of contracts including not limited to HDM licensing and training (US$1 million) and (ii) a capacity building program on climate resilient asset management including a gender focused training programme for young professionals to build experience towards providing support

wbg_operations.amount_basis: World Bank original commitment (USD), whole operation; not allocated to clusters
wbg_operations.description: The development objective of the  Oromia National Regional State Forested Landscape Project for Ethiopia is to improve the enabling environment for sustainable forest managementand investment in Oromia. The project has three components. First component, enabling investments will finance investment in PFM (including livelihoods support and selected nature-based community enterprise development) and reforestation in deforestation hotspots insites to be selected, as well as extension services and land-use planning statewide at state and local levels. Second component, enabling environment will finance complementary activities to improve the effectiveness andimpact of institutions, policies, marketing, BSM, and information (that is, strategiccommunication, MRV), and safeguards management at state and local levels. This component will enhance the enabling environment to help scale up and leverage action on the ground toreduce deforestation and forest degradation. Third component, emission reduction payments will be made only for emission reductions achieved during the ERPA period. However, interventions conducive to emission reductions can start at any time. ER payments will be delivered once results are achieved,verified by a third party, and formally reported to the Bank. In addition, the ER payments will not cover the full cost of implementing changes in landscape management. The ER payments will provide some return that offsets some costs of improving the landscape for the wider benefitof all.

wbg_operations.title: Uganda Skills Development in Refugee and Host Communities
wbg_operations.amount_basis: World Bank original commitment (USD), whole operation; not allocated to clusters
wbg_operations.description: Over the last decade, Uganda has made progress in enhancing the skills of the youth population to improve their labor market outcomes, livelihood, and wellbeing. Yet there is still an urgency to address this issue particularly in refugee and host communities (RHCs) where the disadvantage youth face are pronounced. A large proportion of refugees come from areas with high incidence of civil unrest, extreme poverty and health-related crises. Many of them arrive with limited assets, social connections and language skills, which make it challenging to flourish in their new settlements. Host Ugandans are not necessarily better off. A large proportion of them have low skill levels and educational attainment, and cope with very limited means to make a living.This project is designed to prepare the learning environment and training programs to foster skills that are indispensable for highly disadvantaged communities with limited resources and training opportunities. The target area will be in the refugee and host communities (RHCs) of Isingiro, Madi-Okollo, and Terego districts. The proposed activity is expected to improve relevance of training opportunities by ensuring that the training institutions are well-equipped for learning and preparing market-oriented competence-based training curriculum. This activity is also expected to improve inclusiveness of training opportunities by ensuring the facilities and programs are particularly useful for young women and youth with physical disabilities.

wbg_operations.title: Development Response to Displacement Impacts Project in the HoA
wbg_operations.amount_basis: World Bank original commitment (USD), whole operation; not allocated to clusters
wbg_operations.sector: FY17 - Agriculture, Fishing and Forestry,FY17 - Energy and Extractives,FY17 - Public Administration,FY17 - Social Protection
wbg_operations.description: The development objective of the Development Response to Displacement Impacts Project for Africa is to improve access to basic social services, expand economic opportunities, and enhance environmental management for communities hosting refugees in the targeted areas of Djibouti, Ethiopia, and Uganda. This project has five components. 1) The first component, Social and Economic Services and Infrastructure, aims to improve access to basic social services and economic infrastructure and improve the service-delivery capacity of local authorities at the target subnational and local levels by financing community and strategic investments as well as capacity-support initiatives. It has two subcomponents as follows: (i) Community Investment Fund; and (ii) Capacity support for local planning and decentralized service delivery. 2) The second component, Sustainable Environmental Management, aims to ensure that environmental and natural resources are carefully and sustainably managed so they can support current and future needs and livelihoods. It has two subcomponents as follows: (i) Integrated natural resources management; and (ii) Access to energy. 3) The third component, Livelihoods Program, seeks to improve livelihoods and increase the incomes of refugee-hosting communities based on a market-system approach. It has two subcomponents as follows: (i) Support to traditional and nontraditional livelihoods; and (ii) Capacity support of community-based organizations for livelihoods. 4) The fourth component, Project Management and Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E), will follow a decentralized approach, using existing government structures at the national, subnational, and local levels and local-level community institutions to be established and or strengthened. 5) The fifth component, Regional support for coordination, capacity and knowledge, aims to support the establishment of the Regional Secretariat on Forced Displacement and Mixed Migration, primarily for the Horn of Africa (HOA), but with relevant linkages to the Great Lakes Initiative.

wbg_operations.title: Food Systems Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa (Phase 3) FSRP
wbg_operations.amount_basis: World Bank original commitment (USD), whole operation; not allocated to clusters
wbg_operations.sector: FY17 - Agriculture, Fishing and Forestry,FY17 - Industry, Trade and Services
wbg_operations.description: The development objectives of the Third Phase of the Food Systems Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa Project for Eastern and Southern Africa, Kenya, Comoros, Malawi, Somalia are to increase resilience of food systems and the Recipient’s preparedness for food insecurity in project areas, and, in case of an eligible crisis or emergency, to respond promptly and effectively to it. The project comprises of six components. The first component, building resilient agricultural production capacity aims to strengthen the productivity and resilience of domestic food production to shocks and stressors by supporting the development and adoption of improved agricultural inputs and services and climate-smart and gender-sensitive farming technologies by producers in the crops, livestock, and fisheries sectors. It consists of following sub-components: (i) quality seed systems and climate-smart technologies for food crops; (ii) livestock sector productivity and safety; (iii) resilient fisheries; and (iv) digital agriculture and information services. The second component, supporting the sustainable development of natural resources for resilient agricultural landscapes aims to promote participatory planning and more sustainable natural resources and irrigation infrastructure management by communities, thus helping build resilience and mitigate the adverse impacts of climate change. It consists of following sub-components: (i) resilient landscape and watershed management; (ii) resilient water management; and (iii) resilient coastal and marine resources management. The third component, getting to market will promote the inclusion of smallholder farmers and rural communities in food crops, livestock, and fisheries value chains and more efficient food markets. It consists of following sub-components: (i) post-harvest, post capture handling and national and regional market links; and (ii) rehabilitation of rural feeder roads for improved market access. The fourth component, promoting a greater focus on food systems resilience in national and regional policymaking will handle cross-cutting policy efforts supporting food systems resilience at the national and regional levels. It consists of following sub-components: (i) strategies, standards, regulations, and institutional framework; (ii) agrifood system stakeholder capacity building; and (iii) regional integration efforts. The fifth component, contingent emergency response component (CERC) will finance eligible expenditures in the event of a disaster-related emergency. The sixth component, project management will support all aspects of project management.
iati_titles: Food Systems Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa (Phase 3) FSRP

wbg_operations.title: Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach
wbg_operations.amount_basis: World Bank original commitment (USD), whole operation; not allocated to clusters
wbg_operations.description: The development objective of the Health Emergency Preparedness, Response, and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA) Project is to strengthen health system resilience and multisectoral preparedness and response to health emergencies in Eastern and Southern Africa. There are four components to the project, the first component being strengthening the preparedness and resilience of regional and national health systems to manage health emergencies. This component will finance capacity strengthening of essential institutions, and activities that directly contribute to the resilience of the health systems to cope with HEs and are complementary to other health systems strengthening (HSS). This will have four subcomponents: (i) multisectoral and cross-border planning, financing, and governance; (ii) health workforce development, including a focus on identifying and addressing gender gaps in career progression; (iii)  access to quality health commodities, including building capacity for local vaccine and pharmaceutical manufacturing, based on the lessons learned from the challenges in accessing COVID-19 vaccines in the region; and (iv) information systems for HEs and the digitalization. The second component is the improving the detection of and response to HEs through a multisectoral approach. the third component is the program management. The component will finance expenditures related to M&E, the program leaning agenda including building a body of evidence on gender in PPR, and program implementation and coordination. Finally, the fourth component is the contingent emergency response component. This component will facilitate access to rapid financing by allowing for the reallocation of uncommitted project funds in the event of a natural disaster in a country, either by a formal declaration of a national emergency or upon a formal request from the government.
iati_titles: Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach

wbg_operations.amount_basis: World Bank original commitment (USD), whole operation; not allocated to clusters
wbg_operations.sector: FY17 - Agriculture, Fishing and Forestry,FY17 - Public Administration,FY17 - Social Protection,FY17 - Water, Sanitation and Waste Management
wbg_operations.description: The objective of the Regional Climate Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa Project is to improve the management of water-related climate impacts in Eastern and Southern Africa, and, in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, to respond promptly and effectively to it. There are five components to the project, the first component being risk management and climate financing. This component includes two subcomponents: climate and disasters risk management, and climate financing. the second component is the infrastructure investments and sustainable asset management for climate resilience. This component includes three subcomponents: enhancing institutional capacity for long-term climate risk management, closing the climate resilient infrastructure gap, and sustainable asset management. The third component is the adaptive climate services for resilient communities. This component includes two subcomponents: empowering communities to manage climate risk, and mainstreaming climate resilience in social protection programs. The fourth component is the project management. Finally, the fifth component is the contingent emergency response component.
